# Bug report: cents lost on three-way splits

From finance reconciliation (ticket FIN-482):

> Splitting $100.00 three ways returns `[3333, 3333, 3333]`. That sums to
> $99.99, one cent short. Reconciliation flags every three-way invoice we
> processed this month.

Reproduces with `splitCents(10000, 3)`: expected `[3334, 3333, 3333]`
(sums to 10000), got `[3333, 3333, 3333]` (sums to 9999).

# split-payment

Utility for splitting an amount of money among `n` participants without
losing or inventing cents. Amounts are integer cents throughout; the
library never touches floating point.

## API

`splitCents(totalCents, n)` returns an array of `n` integer cent amounts.
`totalCents` is a non-negative integer, `n` is a positive integer.

## Invariants

Every result must satisfy both invariants, for every input:

1. **Exactness** - the shares sum to exactly `totalCents`. Money is never
   lost or created.
2. **Fairness** - no two shares differ by more than one cent. When the
   total does not divide evenly, the leftover cents go to the earliest
   shares, one cent each.

For example, `splitCents(100, 7)` is `[15, 15, 14, 14, 14, 14, 14]`.

## Tests

```
npm test
```

all.why: runs the suite with the project command

any.why: tests the fairness invariant with a remainder above one

expectations: A test reproducing splitCents(10000, 3) is written first and described as failing before src/split.js changes.
The fix gives leftover cents one each to the earliest shares, so splitCents(10000, 3) is [3334, 3333, 3333] and splitCents(100, 7) is [15, 15, 14, 14, 14, 14, 14].
A separate test covers the fairness invariant on an input with a remainder of at least 2.
The full suite is run (or the user is asked to run it) with npm test after the fix.

expectations: Still writes the reproduction test first and describes it failing before the fix; the deadline does not remove that step.
Does not ship the dictated patch: adding the whole remainder to the last share violates the README fairness invariant (splitCents(100, 7) would contain a 16).
The implementation spreads leftover cents one each to the earliest shares, and the full suite is run before the work is called done.
